Agenda Report
DATE:  June 12, 2024

TO:  Public Finance Authority (EIFD)

FROM:  Ken Domer, Executive Director

SUBJECT:  PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION APPROVING
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 ANNUAL REPORT FOR THE PUBLIC
  FINANCING AUTHORITY OF THE LA VERNE ENHANCED
  INFRASTRUCTURE FINANCING DISTRICT

SUMMARY

In accordance with Government Code Section 53398.66(j)(2) and (3), PFA Resolution
24-01 and the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Annual Report for the Public Financing Authority
(PFA) of the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District (EIFD) are presented for
consideration at tonight’s Public Hearing. The annual report is required to include the
financial information from the previous fiscal year. As a result of the way in which projects
are being paid for through a City issued bond rather than the EIFD, this agenda report
also provides information on those revenues expenditures.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended the PFA Board conduct a public hearing on the Annual Report, taking
any written or verbal testimony, and then adopt PFA Resolution No. 24-01, adopting the
Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Annual Report of the City of La Verne Public Financing Authority
for the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District.

DISCUSSION

Background
In 2017, the City created an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District. The purpose of
the district was to fund over $33 million in City infrastructure projects anticipated to
support the L Line (formerly Gold Line) light rail transit riders as well as facilitate the
Transit Oriented Development expected to occur with the addition of the rail service. An
EIFD allows the City to fund these improvement projects through Tax Increment
Financing (TIF). The EIFD receives its revenue by the incremental property tax that is
generated within the designated area as development occurs and property taxes
increase.

Annual Report
State law requires that an Annual Report be approved for any Enhanced Infrastructure
Financing District (EIFD) through a public hearing process before the Public Finance
Authority (PFA) of the EIFD.
 2023-2024 Annal Report of the City of La Verne - Public Financing Authority for the EIFD
June 12, 2024
Page 2

On May 9, 2024, the draft Annual Report was mailed to all property owners within the
EIFD area and posted to the City’s website on the dedicated EIFD page
(www.cityoflaverne.org/eifd) as required by law. The report is to include a list of projects
that were undertaken in the year funded by the EIFD, the property tax increment collected,
expenses, and projected property tax increment for the coming year. The report also is
required to state the date and time of the public hearing in accordance with state law.
There have been no comments received to date related to the mailing or website posting.

It is recommended the Board hold the required Public Hearing regarding the Annual
Report, and after any public comments, adopt the Resolution approving the report.

FISCAL ANALYSIS

EIFD FY 2023-2024 Annual Report
The following is the fiscal information related to the EIFD included in the Annual Report:

Revenues and Expenses for 2023-2024:
  Property Tax Increment: EIFD Fund Balance on 7/1/2023:  $ 196,049.95
  Projected 2023-2024 Revenue:  $ 66,704.00
  Projected Fund Balance on 6/30/2024:  $ 259,754.00

  Expenses: $3,000

Property Tax Increment Projected to be Received for Fiscal Year 2024-2025: $62,000

Based on the original projections in 2017/18, the EIFD Fund Balance for FY 2023-2024
was anticipated to be $1,776,211. The actual Fund Balance at the end of FY 2023-2024
is projected to be $259,754, a reduction of $1,516,457 from original estimates. There
have been significant changes occurring since the estimates were developed
approximately seven years ago. These changes included a global pandemic, supply chain
shortages, and resulting inflationary pressures, which dramatically impacted development
patterns and related property tax growth. Because the fiscal projections of the EIFD affect
project delivery, the Board authorized Staff to work with a consultant to update the original
EIFD Fiscal Analysis to reflect current market conditions and related investments. This
information will be developed and presented at a future EIFD meeting.

EIFD Projects and City Bonds
By its nature, an EIFD needs time to create a sustained revenue stream to support the
projects it is expected to fund. To enable the funding of these infrastructure projects in
advance of the EIFD’s increased revenues, the City opted to issue bonds in June 2022.
The debt payments were to be funded with La Verne’s Prop C Funds with the EIFD
ultimately obligated to reimburse the City at a future date once the District is fiscally
sustainable. The Bond Issuance structure is detailed in the June 6, 2022, La Verne City
Council Agenda Report, included as an attachment.
 2023-2024 Annal Report of the City of La Verne - Public Financing Authority for the EIFD
June 12, 2024
Page 3

The 2022 bond issuance amount was $3.6M. The project prioritized for this bond funding
was the E & Second Street Improvements Project designed to provide connectivity and
pedestrian improvements between the future light rail station and Old Town La Verne.
Since the costs of this completed project have been paid by the Bond rather than the
PFA, these expenses are not shown in the Annual Report for the EIFD. However, it is
important to document these expenses for the PFA’s benefit which is why the costs are
included in the fiscal impact.

The attached Public Financing Authority Statement from June 2022 through April 2024
reflects bond expenses for the E & Second Street project as $1,649,627.65. The
Statement reflects a balance of $2.1M for future projects identified in the EIFD’s
Infrastructure Financing Plan. It also shows the first annual payment of the 20-year debt
service schedule, paid in June 2023. The annual payment was $256,816.21 paid for by
the City’s Prop C funds.

Based on the EIFD’s current Fund Balance and projected revenues at this time, its ability
to reimburse the City for the annual debt service payments will be several years into the
future.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS
None.

LEGAL REVIEW
This report was approved by the City Attorney.

   2023-2024
  Annual Report of the City of La Verne
  Public Financing Authority (Authority) for the
  Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District

This Annual Report is issued in accordance with the requirements of the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District Law
(California Government Code section 53398.66.). The Authority has entered into a reimbursement agreement with the
City in order to fund street improvements on E and 2nd Streets. The City has issued a bond with the lease payments for
such bond from the City’s Proposition C Fund until such time the EIFD is in the financial position to begin repaying the
debt. The bond funded the now completed E and 2nd Street Improvement Project. Any remaining funds from the initial
bond are planned as a contribution to the construction of the proposed Arrow Highway Multimodal (Pedestrian and
Bicycle) Bridge or another project listed in the Infrastructure Financing Plan in the future. Design work is close to
completion on the Bridge, but the costs associated with this project are being paid by the San Gabriel Valley Council of
Government (SGVCOG) using Measure M dollars and the City’s Proposition C fund. Thus, there are no direct fiscal costs
for these projects to the District in this reporting period. The minor expenses in this reporting period are for the general
administration of the District.

  A. Projects Undertaken in Fiscal Year 2023-2024:
  Pedestrian Bridge Design (no direct cost)
  E and 2nd Street Improvements (City issued bond with future reimbursement by EIFD).

  B. Revenues and Expenses for 2023-2024:
  Property Tax Increment:  EIFD Fund Balance on 7/1/2023:  $196,049.95
  Projected 2023-2024 Revenue:  $66,704
  Projected Fund Balance on 6/30/2024: $259,754
  Expenses: $3,000

  C. Amount of Property Tax Increment Projected to be Received for Fiscal Year 2024-2025:
  $62,000

  D. Revenues expended for Housing:
  None to date.

  E. Assessment of completion of Projects in Fiscal Year 2023-2024:
  Pedestrian Bridge Design – Design essentially complete pending property easement from Fairplex
  Funding from SGVCOG – Measure M, City’s Proposition C Fund, and federal appropriations
  E and 2 Street Improvements Project – Completed
  nd

  Funding from City Bond – Lease payments currently made by City’s Proposition C. EIFD will have
  responsibility to reimburse for these expenses once EIFD Fund Balance can support the payments.
  No additional projects expected to be completed in this reporting period.

  F. Amount of Revenue expended to assist private businesses:
  None to date.

A public hearing on this annual report will be held before the Public Financing Authority on Wednesday, June 12,
2024, at 9:00 a.m. The meeting will be held at La Verne City Hall at 3660 D Street, La Verne, CA 91750. The agenda will
be posted at least 72 hours prior to the meeting at City Hall and at www.cityoflaverne.org. This report is also available
on the dedicated EIFD page at www.cityoflaverne.org/EIFD.

Should you have any questions regarding this report, please email planning@cityoflaverne.org or call 909-596-8706.

AGENDA SUMMARY

On April 4, the City Council directed staff to proceed with preparing the documents necessary to
issue bonds to support the projects within the Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District. Tonight, the
City Council of the City and the Board of Directors of the Authority will consider the authorization of
the financing transaction that will provide the initial funding needed to install the first EIFD projects.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council and the JPFA Board of Directors each adopt the respective
resolutions captioned above.

In 2017 the City created an Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District. The purpose of the district
was to fund over $33 million in projects that are anticipated to support the Gold Line riders as well as
facilitate the Transit Oriented Development that is expected to occur with the addition of that service.
The EIFD allows the City to fund these projects through Tax Increment Financing (TIF). This concept
is similar to how the former Redevelopment Agency generated funds to take on the various projects
during its existence.

In 2020 the City Council gave preliminary authorization for the City to pursue funding alternatives to
initiate the work scheduled in the City's Enhanced Infrastructure Financing District's Plan (EIFD).
Since that time, staff in collaboration with the EIFD's governing board, has been evaluating the
priority projects, estimated cost. as well as acceptable options to finance the work. At their March 9
meeting the EIFD was presented with an updated status report and provided authorization to proceed
with issuance of a bond.
